column7: Branches on config.mtls.enabled to choose the mTLS listener (super::support::serve_tls) versus a plain cleartext axum_server listener, so a mistake serves cleartext when client-cert auth was configured.
Refuses an HTTP start whose firewall anomaly config has no key (refuse_keyless_http_anomaly) with Error::Config, a startup refusal on a security ground.

Wires the events hub, webhook registry, kill-switch source and the upstream_live_ineligible gate and live credentials into meta_mcp; a mistake would silently drop those checks, but it decides nothing itself (EventsHub and upstream_live_ineligible decide).
Logs the startup banner and prints the dashboard link only when dashboard_link (critical d) returns one; a mistake that prints a link of its own silently leaks the admin-granting value.
Stores the mTLS client identity that the per-connection service later checks and injects; a mistake would silently drop or swap the identity.

Clones the connection's CertIdentity into each PeerCertIdentityService; decision is made in PeerCertIdentityService::call, a mistake would silently run requests without the nameless-cert check or identity.
Refuses every request on a connection whose client certificate names no subject (unauthenticated response) and otherwise binds the verified cert identity into request extensions.
Refuses startup when server.replicas > 1 with per-process state (key_server tokens/revocations) where a revoke would reach only one replica.
Wires config.tasks per-principal, record and byte limits (StoreLimits) and the shared admission authority into the task runtime; a mistake would silently disable the limits enforced by TaskService.
Seals the executor via cancel_remaining so no task starts against a closing store (the refusal lives in TaskExecutor); a mistake would silently reopen task admission during teardown.
Decides whether server.public_url names a non-loopback host, which makes the listener network-exposed and so subject to the cleartext-credential refusal.
Extracts the host from server.public_url that network_exposure and service_host decide on; a parse mistake would silently skip the cleartext refusal.
Decides whether the listener is reachable off-machine (public_url host or non-loopback bind), the precondition for cleartext_credential_refusal to refuse.
Decides whether public_url names a Kubernetes Service, which lets cluster_internal cleartext HTTP through instead of being refused.
Resolves which directory holds the governance store and audit log; a wrong path would silently relocate or share governance state, while build_control_plane_store enforces the absolute-path check.
Refuses start for a relative or unwritable store_dir, disables governance mutations when auth is off (anonymous-admin surface), and refuses when identity grants lack the audit log.
Proves an explicit store directory is writable using unlink plus create_new so a planted symlink cannot redirect the write, and returns failure that refuses start.
Builds the governance audit log config with the signing identity and bounded rotation; a mistake would silently leave governance audit entries unsigned or unbounded.
Opens the governance audit log and file store, classifying lease-held versus other failures; build_control_plane_store decides whether the failure refuses start.
Builds the sink that publishes identity grants on reload (None when grants are off); a mistake would silently stop reloaded grants from taking effect.
Loads the identity grants that bind callers to capabilities and, when fail_on_error is set, refuses start on an unreadable file; otherwise fails closed with no grants.

Opens the governance store for stdio and runs the startup grant audit; a mistake would silently serve stdio without audited grants, while build_control_plane_store and start_identity_grant_audit decide refusals.
Resolves the provenance signing key and key id through the env overlay; a mistake would silently leave the signer uninstalled or keyed wrongly.
Fails closed by refusing to install a signer for an empty or whitespace key (forgeable signatures) and derives the domain-separated receipt subkey.

Reports that warm-start admission is sealed after shutdown, so no new warm-start task contacts a backend once teardown has begun; a shutdown gate on backend contact (W6 CustodyHandle::provider precedent).
Withholds the admin-granting dashboard link unless auth is on, the bind is loopback and a bootstrap value exists, so a network listener's shipped log never carries it.

Decides whether callers with access to a backend hear a tools/list_changed after a nudge, by comparing a fingerprint of the shared visible list; it does not consult per-caller tool visibility, so a change to a tool hidden from a caller still notifies it (timing side channel, MIK-8350).

Decides whether a capability catalogue change is announced, by comparing a fingerprint of its listed tools; it does not consult per-caller visibility, so a hidden capability's change still notifies (MIK-8350).
Schedules warm-ups under the warmer lock only while closed() (critical d) reports admission open; a mistake that skips the check silently lets warm-start contact backends during teardown.
Applies a reload's backend set to the warmer only while closed() (critical d) reports admission open; a mistake that skips the check silently schedules backend contact after shutdown.
